title: No secret to lose
sub: The second film of Locks before the data, the first series of Data protection and privacy: why a sign-in secret is bearer paper, as the City of London's money markets learned in 1990; the ways a job proves who it is, ranked by who holds a secret and for how long, up to an identity the platform gives it; and the same ladder for people, up to a passkey that answers only the real site.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's look, Night glass: a dark hall of frosted panes, frosted where what's behind may not be read and clear where it may, with cards of near-clear frost and bright rims. Cyan is an identity, green allowed, coral denied or closed; a secret is always a sealed card of violet frost with a lock, never written out. The City of London of 1990 is painted in the same night light, with its place and year on a tag.
